title: '6g Cocaine & Whiskey In 3 Hours': Influencer Dies In New Year Challenge, Mom Finds Him 'Unconscious' | Viral News - News18
text: An influencer in Barcelona, Spain, lost his life during a New Year’s Eve live challenge. It involved dangerous levels of drugs and alcohol. The influencer, Sergio Jiménez Ramos, 37, was found dead in his home in Vilanova i la Geltrú, southwest of Barcelona, after he reportedly took part in an extreme livestream for paying viewers. Known online as Sancho or Sssanchopanza, Jiménez had built a following on the streaming platforms Kick and Twitch, where he participated in viral challenges and stunts requested by donors. While these broadcasts were intended as entertainment for a private audience, the challenge he attempted on the night of December 31 ended tragically. ‘6g Cocaine And Bottle Of Whiskey In 3 Hours’: Dangerous Livestreams For Money According to Spanish media outlets El País and El Periódico, Jiménez had promised to consume six grams of cocaine and an entire bottle of whisky within three hours, all as part of a private video call for viewers who had bought him the drugs and paid to watch him perform the challenge. This livestream, though private, was part of a trend in which some content creators engage in extreme behaviour in exchange for financial donations. Spanish Influencer Was Found Dead By Family Jiménez lived with his mother, Teresa, who discovered something was wrong in the early hours of January 1. She told El Periódico de Catalunya, “I asked him what he was doing, but he didn’t answer." Teresa saw his bedroom door slightly open and tried to push it, but something was blocking it. Alarmed, she called her other sons, and Daniel arrived quickly. He forced his way into the room and found Jiménez kneeling on the floor next to his bed, “as if in prayer." His head was resting against the mattress, and his hand tightly held the phone, which was still livestreaming, he recounted to El Periódico. Nearby, Daniel saw a nearly empty bottle of whisky, two energy drink cans and a small pile of cocaine on a strip of red paper. The livestream reportedly continued to capture viewers’ voices in the background, with comments such as: “Are you sleeping off your hangover yet Sergio? Haven’t you finished your bottle of whisky?" Police Investigation The Mossos d’Esquadra, Catalonia’s police force, have launched an investigation into Jiménez’s death and has ordered an autopsy, according to El País. While the police have not made a public statement about the death, they have taken the opportunity to issue a broader warning about the dangers of online challenges. On January 6, the Mossos posted a video on social media to caution people about participating in trends that could endanger life or physical integrity. As one officer said in Spanish in the video: “The consequences of these trends can range from intoxication to physical and psychological effects, and can also have a negative impact on their reputation, affecting job and academic opportunities due to the digital footprint left behind. It’s important to be aware that some trends can have consequences if they involve acts of vandalism or aggression." Jiménez’s Extreme Challenges Inspired By Simón Pérez Jiménez had just turned 37 on December 13 and was reportedly attempting to emulate other influencers who had risen to fame through risky, often drug-fueled challenges. El País notes that he drew inspiration from Simón Pérez, a Spanish influencer known for making viral videos involving substance use in front of paying audiences. Jiménez reportedly created his own spinoff content after appearing alongside Pérez in October.
